In an interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and his vision for a tab-less interface. The full interview can be watched below.

Work feature may soon be seamlessly integrated with ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern released a teaser clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern published the full interview, covering the new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the lawsuit with Apple, and the recent Hugging Face breach.

During the interview, Stern mentioned OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, along with the launch of ChatGPT's new agent mode, Work.

The merged interface has caused confusion for users, especially those who just want to continue using ChatGPT but are struggling to find their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top of the interface and a dropdown menu in the left sidebar to make it easier to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app has become less difficult to operate, the interface remains somewhat overly complex.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, acknowledging that the new interface was "indeed a bit messy," but added that this is a "phased step toward the future," and that the Work tab will eventually disappear, with its features being "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also noted that despite the confusing deployment process during the app merger, OpenAI still achieved the expected results, with Codex's user base doubling from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth stemmed from forcing Codex "down the throat" of the ChatGPT app, Brockman again acknowledged this, while also arguing that this was to some extent their goal all along:

The full interview is rich in content and absolutely worth watching. The interview also includes a segment very much in "Joanna Stern style," where she attempts to incorporate the ChatGPT voice feature into the conversation, with results exactly as you might imagine.
